lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Personal details such as date of birth and nationality should be removed from the résumé.
items.because: Readers are not meant to weigh these details, and they use scarce space while introducing irrelevant personal information.

items.says: The résumé repeats the same onboarding achievement under Harbor Payments and the hospital practicum with conflicting context and results.
items.because: The hospital attribution and the conflict between “9 days to 4” and “halved” create doubt about ownership and accuracy.

items.says: EXPERIENCE should appear above EDUCATION.
items.because: Leading with education may cause recruiters to miss the operations and product direction established by more than four years of full-time work.

items.says: The résumé has an unexplained eight-month gap between the undergraduate degree and the first listed role.
items.because: A recruiter may wonder whether a job, relocation, study period or other relevant activity is missing.

items.says: The checkout-conversion claim is not established for all merchants merely by replacing the flow.
items.because: A before-and-after result cannot separate the flow’s effect from seasonality, traffic mix, instrumentation changes or other factors without a controlled comparison.

items.says: The checkout-conversion bullet does not identify the baseline or comparison period behind the 35% figure.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether 35% is a relative increase or a change from one conversion rate to another.

items.says: The checkout-conversion bullet should present the measured population rather than claim the result for all merchants.
items.because: The bullet’s evidence does not support its universal scope.

items.says: The dispute self-service bullet gives a delivery milestone but no outcome from the product itself.
items.because: Shipping early proves execution speed but not whether the feature solved a customer or business problem.

items.says: The chargeback-loss result is stated indirectly, and the dollar figure is not in a scannable résumé format.
items.because: The roadmap impact comes after too much setup, and “1.1 million dollars” is slower to scan than an abbreviated figure.

items.says: The triage bullet uses vague timing filler and gives the queue reduction without its starting or ending count.
items.because: “Over the summer” adds little beyond the internship dates, while a relative reduction without counts makes the scale harder to judge.

items.says: The onboarding comparison cannot establish that the redesign caused improvement because merchants self-selected into the flows.
items.because: Adopters and non-adopters may have differed before the redesign, so the comparison supports association rather than causation.

items.says: The onboarding-measurement bullet reports the comparison method but not its outcome.
items.because: The line reads as a measurement process rather than an accomplishment because it does not say whether onboarding improved.

items.says: The phrase describing merchants who opted into the new flow and those who stayed on the old one is unnecessarily long.
items.because: The comparison groups are difficult to scan, and the length competes with the result.

items.says: The 9-days-to-4-days result conflicts with the separate claim that the same redesign halved time to first payment.
items.because: A reduction from 9 days to 4 days is about 55.6%, while an exact halving would be 4.5 days.

items.says: The unit is missing after the ending value in “from 9 days to 4.”
items.because: Without “days” after 4, the comparison is grammatically incomplete and requires the reader to infer the unit.

items.says: The Harbor Payments internship reads as separate tasks instead of a prioritized product story.
items.because: Routine triage and measurement dilute the redesign, roadmap and shipped-product outcomes in an undifferentiated list.

items.says: Excluding weather-delayed shipments changed the reported late-delivery rate but did not cut the underlying number of late deliveries.
items.because: The bullet presents a change in the metric’s denominator as an operational performance improvement.

items.says: “Cut warehouse pick errors 30%” is grammatically incomplete because the reduction needs “by.”
items.because: The missing preposition makes the result read awkwardly and slows a recruiter’s scan.

items.says: The pick-error result gives a percentage reduction without its starting and ending error rates.
items.because: A percentage reduction without a baseline is harder to judge and less credible.

items.says: “Prepares the forecast pack” incorrectly uses present tense for a role that ended in August 2023.
items.because: The tense shift claims the preparation is ongoing and can make the employment timeline seem inaccurate.

items.says: The S&OP review and forecast-pack bullet does not state what changed as a result.
items.because: Without an operating outcome, the line reads mainly as meeting administration.

items.says: “S&OP” is unexplained jargon for readers outside operations and supply-chain functions.
items.because: A recruiter unfamiliar with the abbreviation may not understand that it means sales and operations planning.

items.says: The app-launch bullet does not show what Riley personally did as product lead.
items.because: The scale and outcome are clear, but the product decision or ownership detail that enabled them is not.

items.says: The app’s scope is unclear because “with two dining halls” does not say whether it served students, halls or both.
items.because: A recruiter may misread the relationship between the users and the dining halls.

items.says: The pickup-reminder bullet should not imply that interviews proved the reminders caused user growth.
items.because: The growth could also reflect seasonality, promotion, food-supply changes or other operational changes.

items.says: The volunteer-system bullet does not show what product or operational work Riley owned.
items.because: A reader cannot distinguish designing the process from simply administering an existing arrangement.

items.says: The volunteer-system bullet does not clearly show whether it operated across both dining halls and repeats the weekly time frame.
items.because: The scope is ambiguous, and using both “each week” and “a week” is redundant and awkward.

items.says: The outpatient-scheduling working-session bullet gives no resulting change or measurable outcome.
items.because: Without an outcome, the practicum reads as recurring meetings rather than consulting work.

items.says: “Working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling” does not show what analytical or consulting work Riley led.
items.because: The bullet shows stakeholder access without demonstrating the skill or contribution behind it.

items.says: The patient-intake bullet does not show what the mapping analysis identified or what the shortened form improved.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what was removed, how substantial the reduction was or what operational result followed.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding result does not belong in the regional hospital network practicum.
items.because: Merchant onboarding and first-payment timing are payments-industry processes, and the line duplicates the Harbor Payments claim.

items.says: The phrase “it takes” incorrectly shifts the merchant bullet into present tense.
items.because: The practicum is a completed role, so present tense makes the timing inconsistent.

items.says: The hospital practicum should remove the merchant-payment bullet and lead with the adopted intake improvement.
items.because: The merchant bullet changes industry, duplicates another entry and makes the practicum look copied or factually unreliable.
